**🎯 Today's Goal:**
Your child will be able to set up a chess board completely from memory without any mistakes.

parent_reference.heading: 1. At a Glance
parent_reference.content:
- **Topic**: Initial Position
- **Difficulty**: Beginner
- **Typical age**: 6+
- **Estimated teaching time**: 15 min
- **Piece/concept type**: Rule
- **Prerequisites**: TOP-014 Piece Values, TOP-002 Board Orientation

**🎯 Today's Goal:**
Your child will be able to set up a chess board completely from memory without any mistakes.

**✅ Lesson Success Criteria:**
- The child places the board with a light square in the bottom right corner.
- The child places the Queen on the square matching her dress color.
- The child places all other pieces in their exact starting positions.

*(Purpose: "Can I teach this today?" A quick summary for busy parents.)*

parent_reference.heading: 2. Definition
parent_reference.content: Before every game of chess, the 32 pieces must be placed in a very specific starting formation called the Initial Position. The pawns form a defensive wall on the second rank. Behind them, the heavy pieces sit on the first rank. The board itself must be oriented so that each player has a light-colored square in their bottom right corner. The most critical rule for piece placement is that the Queen always starts on a square that matches her own color.

parent_reference.heading: 3. Why It Matters
parent_reference.content: A game of chess played on an incorrectly set up board is technically invalid! Memorizing the setup is the child's first step toward independence. When they can set up the board by themselves, they feel ownership of the game and are ready to challenge friends and family without needing a parent's help.

parent_reference.heading: 4. Before You Teach (Graph)
parent_reference.content:
- **Requires:** TOP-002 (Board Orientation), TOP-014 (Piece Values)
- **Unlocks:** TOP-016 (Game Phases), TOP-036 (Opening Principles)

parent_reference.heading: 5. Parent Understands
parent_reference.content:
Setting up the board is a ritual. 
1. **The Board:** Always check the bottom right corner nearest to you. It MUST be a light square ("White on right"). If it's a dark square, rotate the board 90 degrees.
2. **The Pawns:** All 8 pawns go on the second row (Rank 2 for White, Rank 7 for Black).
3. **The Outside-In Method:** It is easiest to place the back row from the outside corners moving inward: Rooks in the corners, then Knights, then Bishops.
4. **The Royals:** You will be left with two center squares. The Queen goes on the square that matches her color (White Queen on Light square, Black Queen on Dark square). The King takes the last remaining square.

parent_reference.heading: 6. How to Teach It
parent_reference.content:
1. **The Blank Canvas:** Start with an empty board. Ask the child to check the bottom right corner. Teach the rhyme: "Light on right!"
2. **The Infantry Wall:** Give the child the 8 White pawns. Tell them to build a wall on the second road.
3. **The Castles:** "Where do you build castle towers?" In the corners! Place the Rooks on `a1` and `h1`.
4. **The Horses:** "The horses live right next to the castle." Place the Knights on `b1` and `g1`.
5. **The Wizards:** "The wizards stand next to the horses to give them magic." Place the Bishops on `c1` and `f1`.
6. **The Queen's Dress:** "The Queen is very fashionable. Her dress must match her shoes!" Place the White Queen on the light square (`d1`).
7. **The King's Throne:** "The King takes whatever seat is left." Place the King on `e1`.

parent_reference.heading: 7. Teaching Story / Analogy / Memory Hint
parent_reference.content:
**The Royal Portrait:** 
Imagine we are setting up a family photo for the kingdom! We build the pawn fence first. Then we put the big heavy castles on the outside edges of the photo so it looks even. The horses want to stand next to the castles, and the magic wizards stand next to the horses. Finally, in the very middle, the King and Queen stand together. And remember, the Queen is so fancy, she demands a carpet that perfectly matches her dress!

parent_reference.heading: 8. Did You Know? 🎓
parent_reference.content: In the initial position, the White King and the Black King always face each other exactly on the same file (the `e` file). If your King is staring at the enemy Queen across the board, somebody set the board up backwards!

parent_reference.heading: 9. Board Diagram 1 — Basic Concept
parent_reference.content:
![DGM-015-01: An empty board with the bottom right square highlighted in bright green, labeled "Light on Right".](../../assets/diagrams/TOP-015/DGM-015-01.svg)
*Step 1: Always check the bottom right corner. Light on Right!*

parent_reference.heading: 10. How It Works
parent_reference.content: Symmetry is your best friend when setting up the board. The left side of your army mirrors the right side of your army, until you get to the King and Queen. The two armies also mirror each other across the board (White's Queen is on the `d` file, and Black's Queen is also on the `d` file facing her directly).

parent_reference.heading: 11. Board Diagram 2 — Practical Example
parent_reference.content:
![DGM-015-02: The complete back row setup showing Rooks, Knights, Bishops, Queen on color, and King.](../../assets/diagrams/TOP-015/DGM-015-02.svg)
*The Queen matches her color. The King takes what is left.*

parent_reference.heading: 12. Real Game Example
parent_reference.content:
![DGM-015-03: The complete Initial Position with all 32 pieces perfectly set up.](../../assets/diagrams/TOP-015/DGM-015-03.svg)
*The final setup. Every game of chess in the world starts exactly like this.*

parent_reference.heading: 13. Common Mistakes
parent_reference.content:
- **Board sideways:** The most common mistake. A dark square in the bottom right corner flips the colors for the King and Queen!
- **King and Queen swapped:** Placing the White Queen on the dark square.
- **Knights and Bishops swapped:** Placing Bishops in the corners or next to the Rooks.

> **🧑‍🏫 Coach Tip:**
> If your child swaps the King and Queen, point at the White Queen and say in a silly voice, "Excuse me! My dress is white and I am standing in dark mud! This is unacceptable!"

parent_reference.heading: 14. Teaching Notes
parent_reference.content:
Make setting up the board a physical race. Children love tactile speed challenges. Do not help them unless they are truly stuck. It is better for them to make a mistake and have you do a "Quality Inspection" at the end.

> **🧑‍🏫 Coach Tip:**
> When inspecting their setup, use the "Two checks" method. Point to the bottom right corner: "Check one: Light on right?" Point to the Queens: "Check two: Dress matches the floor?" If both are yes, the board is usually correct.

parent_reference.heading: 15. Parent FAQ
parent_reference.content:
**Q: Does it matter which Knight goes on which side?**
A: No! Both White Knights are identical. Both White Rooks are identical. You can place them on either side.

**Q: Do I always have to play White?**
A: You should trade colors every game! But notice that the rule is the same for Black: Black's bottom right corner will ALSO be a light square!

parent_reference.heading: 16. Practice Together
parent_reference.content:
**The Setup Race:**
Take all the pieces and dump them in a pile in the middle of the table. You take the Black pieces, and your child takes the White pieces. Say "Ready, Set, Go!" and race to see who can set up their side of the board the fastest. When you both finish, inspect each other's boards for the "Queen's Dress" mistake!

parent_reference.heading: 17. Coach Challenge ⭐
parent_reference.content:
**The Detective:**
Have your child close their eyes. You (the parent) set up the entire board, but deliberately make TWO mistakes. (For example, swap a Knight and a Bishop, and place the Queen on the wrong color). Tell your child to open their eyes and be a Detective. Can they find and fix the two mistakes before the game starts?

parent_reference.heading: 18. Try It Yourself
parent_reference.content:
### 🟢 Recognition (Easy)
![DGM-015-04: An empty board. The bottom right square is dark.](../../assets/diagrams/TOP-015/DGM-015-04.svg)
**Question:** Look at the bottom right corner. Is this board ready to play, or do we need to turn it?
**Answer:** Turn it! The bottom right corner must be a LIGHT square!

### 🟡 Application (Medium)
![DGM-015-05: White's back rank. Rooks on a1/h1. Knights on c1/f1. Bishops on b1/g1.](../../assets/diagrams/TOP-015/DGM-015-05.svg)
**Question:** Look closely at the horses and the wizards. Did someone make a mistake?
**Answer:** Yes! The Knights (horses) should be next to the Rooks, and the Bishops (wizards) should be next to the King and Queen!

### 🔴 Challenge (Hard)
![DGM-015-06: White King on d1 (light square). White Queen on e1 (dark square).](../../assets/diagrams/TOP-015/DGM-015-06.svg)
**Question:** What is wrong with the King and Queen in this picture?
**Answer:** The White Queen is standing on a dark square! She needs to move to d1 so her dress matches the floor, and the King moves to e1.

parent_reference.heading: 19. Continue Learning
parent_reference.content: - **Lichess Practice:** [Board Setup](https://lichess.org/learn#/8) (Interactive drills).

parent_reference.heading: 20. Related Topics
parent_reference.content:
- **Prerequisites:** TOP-014 Piece Values
- **Next Steps:** TOP-017 Algebraic Notation, TOP-016 Game Phases

parent_reference.heading: 21. Parent Confidence Check ✅
parent_reference.content:
- [ ] Do I know the rule "Light on right"?
- [ ] Do I know the rule "Queen on her own color"?
- [ ] Can my child set up the board without asking for help?
- [ ] Did we play the "Setup Race" game?

> When inspecting their setup, use the "Two checks" method. Point to the bottom right corner: "Check one: Light on right?" Point to the Queens: "Check two: Dress matches the floor?" If both are yes, the board is usually correct.

**Q: Does it matter which Knight goes on which side?**
A: No! Both White Knights are identical. Both White Rooks are identical. You can place them on either side.

**Q: Do I always have to play White?**
A: You should trade colors every game! But notice that the rule is the same for Black: Black's bottom right corner will ALSO be a light square!

**🎯 Today's Goal:**
Your child will be able to set up a chess board completely from memory without any mistakes.

**✅ Lesson Success Criteria:**
- The child places the board with a light square in the bottom right corner.
- The child places the Queen on the square matching her dress color.
- The child places all other pieces in their exact starting positions.

*(Purpose: "Can I teach this today?" A quick summary for busy parents.)*

sections.title: Definition
sections.text: Before every game of chess, the 32 pieces must be placed in a very specific starting formation called the Initial Position. The pawns form a defensive wall on the second rank. Behind them, the heavy pieces sit on the first rank. The board itself must be oriented so that each player has a light-colored square in their bottom right corner. The most critical rule for piece placement is that the Queen always starts on a square that matches her own color.

sections.title: Why It Matters
sections.text: A game of chess played on an incorrectly set up board is technically invalid! Memorizing the setup is the child's first step toward independence. When they can set up the board by themselves, they feel ownership of the game and are ready to challenge friends and family without needing a parent's help.

sections.title: Before You Teach (Graph)
sections.text:

- **Unlocks:** TOP-016 (Game Phases), TOP-036 (Opening Principles)

sections.title: Parent Understands
sections.text:
Setting up the board is a ritual. 
1. **The Board:** Always check the bottom right corner nearest to you. It MUST be a light square ("White on right"). If it's a dark square, rotate the board 90 degrees.
2. **The Pawns:** All 8 pawns go on the second row (Rank 2 for White, Rank 7 for Black).
3. **The Outside-In Method:** It is easiest to place the back row from the outside corners moving inward: Rooks in the corners, then Knights, then Bishops.
4. **The Royals:** You will be left with two center squares. The Queen goes on the square that matches her color (White Queen on Light square, Black Queen on Dark square). The King takes the last remaining square.

sections.title: How to Teach It
sections.text:
1. **The Blank Canvas:** Start with an empty board. Ask the child to check the bottom right corner. Teach the rhyme: "Light on right!"
2. **The Infantry Wall:** Give the child the 8 White pawns. Tell them to build a wall on the second road.
3. **The Castles:** "Where do you build castle towers?" In the corners! Place the Rooks on `a1` and `h1`.
4. **The Horses:** "The horses live right next to the castle." Place the Knights on `b1` and `g1`.
5. **The Wizards:** "The wizards stand next to the horses to give them magic." Place the Bishops on `c1` and `f1`.
6. **The Queen's Dress:** "The Queen is very fashionable. Her dress must match her shoes!" Place the White Queen on the light square (`d1`).
7. **The King's Throne:** "The King takes whatever seat is left." Place the King on `e1`.

sections.title: Teaching Story / Analogy / Memory Hint
sections.text:
**The Royal Portrait:** 
Imagine we are setting up a family photo for the kingdom! We build the pawn fence first. Then we put the big heavy castles on the outside edges of the photo so it looks even. The horses want to stand next to the castles, and the magic wizards stand next to the horses. Finally, in the very middle, the King and Queen stand together. And remember, the Queen is so fancy, she demands a carpet that perfectly matches her dress!

sections.title: Did You Know? 🎓
sections.text: In the initial position, the White King and the Black King always face each other exactly on the same file (the `e` file). If your King is staring at the enemy Queen across the board, somebody set the board up backwards!

sections.title: How It Works
sections.text: Symmetry is your best friend when setting up the board. The left side of your army mirrors the right side of your army, until you get to the King and Queen. The two armies also mirror each other across the board (White's Queen is on the `d` file, and Black's Queen is also on the `d` file facing her directly).

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.text:
- **Board sideways:** The most common mistake. A dark square in the bottom right corner flips the colors for the King and Queen!
- **King and Queen swapped:** Placing the White Queen on the dark square.
- **Knights and Bishops swapped:** Placing Bishops in the corners or next to the Rooks.

> **🧑‍🏫 Coach Tip:**
> If your child swaps the King and Queen, point at the White Queen and say in a silly voice, "Excuse me! My dress is white and I am standing in dark mud! This is unacceptable!"
